page: Google Cloud Platform a2-highgpu-8g is an accelerator-optimized server configured with eight NVIDIA Ampere A100 GPUs providing a total of 320 GB of VRAM. The host system features 96 vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor running at 2.2 GHz across 48 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. System memory totals 680.0 GB, yielding approximately 7.08 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance tradeoff between single-core and multi-core or accelerated workloads. Single-core CPU metrics, such as stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores, fall into the bottom 25% tier. Conversely, multi-core CPU performance is strong, and memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, with read-only cached small block speeds reaching 4215.1 GB/sec. The server demonstrates top-tier performance in large-language model inference, particularly for prompt processing across small, medium, and large models, as well as text generation for medium and large models.

Given the high density of dedicated GPU and memory resources, this server type represents a specialized hardware profile where cost efficiency is realized through parallel processing capabilities rather than general-purpose compute. The lack of local storage requires external storage integration, which must be factored into architectural designs. The server is highly suited for deep learning, large-scale LLM inference, ray tracing, and high-throughput memory-bound operations, but is inefficient for single-threaded tasks.
description: Google Cloud Platform a2-highgpu-8g is an accelerator-optimized server designed for highly parallelized workloads. It features eight NVIDIA Ampere A100 GPUs with 320 GB of total VRAM, paired with 96 vCPUs on an Intel Xeon x86_64 architecture and 680.0 GB of system memory. While single-core CPU benchmarks are weak, the server delivers strong multi-core performance and exceptional memory bandwidth, exceeding 4215 GB/sec in cached read tests. It achieves top-tier results in LLM inference prompt processing and text generation across various model sizes. Lacking local storage, this instance is optimized for GPU-accelerated tasks such as deep learning, large-scale AI inference, and ray tracing, offering high resource density for parallel computing workloads.
